newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds fall off, spreads narrow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds fall off, spreads narrow.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities were broadly weaker with Treasuries, but yield spreads tightened modestly in an abbreviated session on Thursday, traders and analysts said.
At 1500 EST/2000 GMT, pass-through prices were 3/32 to 20/32 lower overall, while comparable Treasuries were down 18/32 to 28/32.
"As (Treasury) prices continue to dive, mortgages keep looking attractive," said one trader in New York.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent paper was off 19/32 at 100-07/32 bid, yielding 136 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were 19/32 lower as well, at 100-06/32 bid and 100-12/32 bid, respectively.
The five-year Treasury note was down 18/32 at 99-11/32 bid to yield 6.78 percent, while the 10-year Treasury note was off 28/32 to yield 6.91 percent.
PSA The Bond Market Trade Association recommended an early close at 1400 EST/1900 GMT Thursday and a full close Friday.
Going forward, mortgages will likely respond in step with Treasuries, said BZW Securities Inc mortgage analyst Cynthia Rivera.

"A huge (Treasury) sell-off like this is going to continue to be better for mortgages or any spread products that have call options," Rivera said. "You are going to see a continued tightening in spreads, but not drastically," she added.
